subject: general
question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct?

63 ÷ 3 × 21 - 15 + 12 = 6
solution: Here, we use the BODMAS table given below: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e10e3be1476caf1bd7e2e109842e7c57ce86da0c54b1b539e233e4e6a7748a44.png] Given: ⇒ 63 ÷ 3 × 21 - 15 + 12 = 6 (1) - and + ⇒ 63 ÷ 3 × 21 - 15 + 12 = 6 After changing the signs: ⇒ __**63 ÷ 3**__ × 21 + 15 - 12 Apply BODMAS rule: ⇒ __**21 × 21**__ + 15 - 12 ⇒ __**441 + 15**__ - 12 ⇒ 456 - 12 = 444
